sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Rusia

The petitioners have filed this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India challenging the notification No. 2723() dated 18.06.2025 published in the Gazette of India whereby the Commissioner, Indore Division has been appointed as Arbitrator under Section 20(F)(6) of the Railways Act, 1989 [Amendment Act, 2008].
2.
Brief facts of the case are that petitioners are resident of village Sultanpur and Semalipura, Tehsil Sardarpur, District Dhar.
They are the owners of agricultural land.

Respondent No. 1 issued a notification dated 08.04.2022 for acquisition of land for laying down Dahod-Indore New BG NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17609 2 WP-24317-2025 Line as a special railway project.

The notification was published in the Gazette of India on 26.06.2024 for acquisition of the land of village Sultanpur and Semalipura under Section 20A of Railways Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 1989').
Respondent No. 1 has also published a notification under Section 20E of the Act, 1989 on 24.12.2024 mentioning the names of land owners and their survey numbers for the purpose of acquisition.

According to the petitioner, this special railway project was started by the Central Government in the year 2014-15 for which lands of Tehsil Sardarpur, District Dhar were acquired under the provisions of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Mukesh vs Ministry Of Railways on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182605923/
1 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 2013').
After publication of the notification, petitioners were issued show-cause notice for submission of objections in respect of the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioners have submitted their objections and thereafter the Land Acquisition Officer has passed the award dated 03.03.2025 for compensation to the petitioners.

Now, the respondent No.1/Ministry of Railways has appointed the Commissioner,
Indore Division as Arbitrator vide impugned notification dated 18.06.2025 as the petitioners and other land owners have a remedy to file applications before the Arbitrator against the award dated 03.03.2025.
3. Petitioners have approached this Court contending that the respondents be directed to acquire the land under the Act of 2013 and not under the Railways Act, 1989.

The scope of interference under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17609 3 WP-24317-2025 of 1996') is very limited whereas the petitioners will have the opportunity file a reference for enhancement of compensation.
In the year 2019, respondent acquired the land under the Act of 2013 for the same project, therefore there cannot be a discrimination between the similarly placed persons.

4. By way of Act No. 11 of 2008, the Government of India inserted Chapter IV A in the Railways Act,
1989 in respect of Land Acquisition for a Special Railway Project with effect from 31.01.2008.
Section 20A of the Act, 1989 empowers the Central Government and prescribes the procedure to acquire any land for execution of a special railway project.

As per Section 20C, there is a provision for payment of compensation for the damages caused while carrying out the work of land such as survey, digging or boring sub-soil, etc. particularly relating to land which is excluded from acquisition proceedings.
Under Section 20D, there is a provision for submission of objection to the competent authority in writing in respect of the acquisition proceedings.

As per Section 20E, where no objection under sub-section (1) of Section 20D has been made within the period specified therein or where the competent authority has disallowed the objections under sub-section (2), the competent authority shall report to the Central Government and thereafter the Central Government by way of notification shall declare that the land should be acquired for the purpose mentioned in sub-section (1) of Section 20A.
On publication of declaration, the land shall be absolutely vested in the Central Government.
5. Section 20F provides for determination of amount payable at compensation.

Where any land is acquired under this Act, the competent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17609 4 WP-24317-2025 authority is required to pass an award within a period of one year from the date of publication of the declaration.
Section 20G provides criterion for determination of market value of the land.
Section 20H provides for deposit and payment of compensation and Section 20-I provides power to take possession.

6. As per sub-section (6) of Section 20F, if the amount determined by the competent authority is not acceptable to either of the parties, on an application filed by either of the parties, the amount shall be determined by the Arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government in such manner for which the provision of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 shall apply.

Sub-section 8 of Section 20F provides that the competent authority or the Arbitrator while determining the amount of Mukesh vs Ministry Of Railways on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182605923/
2 compensation shall take into account the market value of the land, compensation for incidental damage, etc.

Sub-section (9) provides that in addition to the market-value of the land, the competent authority or Arbitrator, as the case may be, in every case shall award a sum of sixty percent on such market value in consideration of the compulsory nature of the acquisition.

7. Therefore, when special provisions have been provided under the Railways Act, 1989 by way of Chapter IV A which is a complete code in itself, the respondent has rightly issued notification and thereafter passed the award for acquisition of land of the petitioners for laying down the railway line under the special railway project.
Therefore, the contention of the petitioners that the respondents be directed to acquire the land under the Act of 2013 cannot be accepted.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17609 5 WP-24317-2025 8.
Further, in exercise of power conferred under Section 20P of the Act of 1989, the rules namely Land Acquisition (Special Railway Projects) Rules, 2016 have been framed.

Rule 3 provides for appointment of arbitrator whereby the Central Government shall, by notification, appoint an officer of the rank of a Gazetted Officer of the State Government as Arbitrator for the purposes of sub-section (6) of Section 20F.
Rule 4 provides for manner of depositing amount with competent authority.

Therefore, in exercise of power conferred under the aforesaid provisions, the Commissioner, Indore Division has been appointed as Arbitrator for this project to decide the application filed under Section 20F (6).

Now that the final award has been passed, the only remedy available to the petitioners is to the challenge the award before the Arbitrator i.e. Commissioner,
Indore Division.
9. In view of the above, we do not find any ground for interference in the impugned notification dated 18.06.2025.
Hence, the petition being devoid of merit stands dismissed.
(VIVEK RUSIA) (BINOD KUMAR
